what: The Quotation Generator creates a professional quote, estimate or proposal that tells a client what the work will cost before it starts. It shows items, discount, tax, other charges, an optional deposit and your terms.
A live preview shows the document as you type. Download a real PDF or print it, and add an “Accepted by” line so the client can sign to approve.
uses: Quote materials and labour before a job.
Send a project estimate with terms.
Give price quotes for bulk orders.
Estimate parts and labour before starting.
tutorial: Type your business name and contact details, add a logo, then the client’s name and details.
Choose the title (Quotation, Estimate, Price quote or Proposal). The number fills in for you. Set the date, how long it is valid and an optional project name.
Type each item with quantity and unit price. Use + Add item for more.
Type a discount and tax rate, any delivery or other charges and an optional deposit percentage.
Describe what is included, timelines and conditions.
Check the preview and press Download PDF or Print. New quote keeps your business details and terms.
features: Quotation, estimate, price quote or proposal.
Worked out from the date and validity period.
Shows the amount needed to start.
For the client to accept the quote.
Long quotes flow onto extra pages.
Drafts and numbering stay in your browser.

example.title: Worked example: a website quote
example.text: Design at 2,400, development at 3,000 and hosting setup at 150 make a subtotal of 5,550. A 5% discount takes off 277.50, 19% tax adds 1,001.78 and there are no other charges, so the total is 6,274.28. A 30% deposit to start is 1,882.28, shown under the total.

tips: Be specific about what is and is not included to avoid disputes.
Set a validity period so old prices do not bind you.
Ask for a deposit on large jobs.
Turn an accepted quote into an invoice with the Invoice Generator.
problems: Type plain numbers. Discount, tax and deposit must be from 0 to 100%.
Set the date, or choose a validity period other than Do not show.
Some letters show as "?" in the PDF
Use Print and choose Save as PDF to keep every script.
